declared_purpose: Read, search, send and manage Outlook mail and calendar through Microsoft Graph using OAuth2. The entry document explicitly includes token refresh, credential storage, token output, mail changes and availability checks (SKILL.md:2-24,32-94,168-187). Supporting code also implements drafts, forwarding, attachment downloads, folder changes, categories, bulk actions and thread searches (scripts/outlook-mail.sh:294-650). These are command-specific paths, not instructions to run every operation.

data_operations.operation: Select an Azure identity and provision an application
data_operations.source: Azure CLI account and application commands; manual Azure Portal instructions
data_operations.data_scope: Account username, application identifiers, display name, account audience, localhost redirect URI and a newly requested two-year client secret. Setup can reuse an existing application before requesting the secret.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Microsoft Azure through Azure CLI or Portal; identifiers and username reach setup output; the client secret enters the local setup process.
data_operations.condition: Automated setup after prerequisites pass, or the corresponding manual setup steps.

data_operations.operation: Configure permissions and exchange an authorization code
data_operations.source: Application configuration, browser authorization and user-entered callback data
data_operations.data_scope: Registration includes Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, Calendars.ReadWrite and User.Read. The authorization/token scope strings contain the first three plus offline_access, excluding User.Read. Automated setup reads the full redirected URL and extracts AUTH_CODE; manual setup requests the code alone. CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET and AUTH_CODE are submitted for token exchange.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Azure application permission configuration; login.microsoftonline.com authorization and token endpoints; localhost browser redirect and local setup input.
data_operations.condition: Initial authorization. Registration configuration does not itself demonstrate that a permission was granted or profile data read.

data_operations.operation: Persist application credentials and token responses
data_operations.source: User-supplied or generated client credentials and token endpoint responses
data_operations.data_scope: Client identifier and client secret in config.json; complete token responses, including access and refresh tokens when supplied, in credentials.json. Refresh replaces the credentials file.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.outlook-mcp/config.json and ~/.outlook-mcp/credentials.json. Setup and manual instructions apply mode 600; refresh does not explicitly reapply permissions.
data_operations.condition: Configuration creation; automated token writes require an access_token field. The manual exchange redirects the response directly to disk. No credential cleanup command is supplied.

data_operations.operation: Read local credentials and optionally return the access token
data_operations.source: Local configuration and credentials files
data_operations.data_scope: Mail and calendar scripts load ACCESS_TOKEN. The token manager loads CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, ACCESS_TOKEN and REFRESH_TOKEN before selecting a command; get prints ACCESS_TOKEN.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local script memory; get returns the token through stdout to its caller. This is explicitly documented token output, with no additional recipient established.
data_operations.condition: Mail/calendar invocation, or any token-manager invocation after its file-existence check.

data_operations.operation: Refresh OAuth tokens
data_operations.source: Locally stored client credentials and REFRESH_TOKEN
data_operations.data_scope: CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, REFRESH_TOKEN and the mail, calendar and offline-access scope string.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token; successful responses replace local credentials.json.
data_operations.condition: Explicit refresh command; errors or status return to the caller.

data_operations.operation: Read inbox statistics and test connectivity
data_operations.source: Microsoft Graph /me/mailFolders/inbox using an access-token bearer header
data_operations.data_scope: An unprojected folder response is received; tests use total and unread counts, while stats also returns the folder name.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local scripts, then statistics or errors through stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Automated setup invokes its test after authorization; manual verification, token test and mail stats are separate paths.

data_operations.operation: List and search mail
data_operations.source: Caller queries, sender addresses and counts; Microsoft Graph message collections
data_operations.data_scope: Search terms or sender filters are sent to Graph. Selected responses contain message IDs, subjects, senders, dates and sometimes read status. Draft lists request recipients and output the first recipient. Displayed message IDs are shortened to their last 20 characters.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: graph.microsoft.com receives authenticated queries; local scripts return projected results to the caller without writing a mail cache.
data_operations.condition: inbox, unread, search, from or drafts command. The inbox path uses /me/messages without an Inbox-folder restriction.

data_operations.operation: Resolve abbreviated message and event identifiers
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied ID suffixes and Graph identifier collections
data_operations.data_scope: Up to 100 message IDs, 50 draft IDs or 50 event IDs per lookup; suffix matching and first-match selection occur locally. The resolved full ID is then used in the target request.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Graph identifiers enter the local process. Subsequent authenticated requests send the selected full ID to Graph.
data_operations.condition: Commands addressing messages, drafts or events by suffix. These lookups support the documented suffix interface; a missing match stops the target operation.

data_operations.operation: Read an email and derive a text excerpt
data_operations.source: Selected Graph message
data_operations.data_scope: Subject, sender name/address, recipient addresses, received time and the body field. HTML stripping and the 2,000-character limit occur locally after receipt.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local curl/jq processing; the projected excerpt and metadata return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: read after successful suffix resolution.

data_operations.operation: List attachments and persist a selected download
data_operations.source: Graph attachment collections and a selected attachment endpoint
data_operations.data_scope: Unprojected attachment lists; list output includes name, size, MIME type and ID. download locally matches a supplied name, fetches the selected contentBytes, decodes it and reports path and size. Failure can print available attachment names.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process and caller output; decoded content is written to OUTPUT/ATT_NAME, defaulting to the current directory. No download cleanup is implemented.
data_operations.condition: attachments lists metadata; download writes only after finding the message and attachment.

data_operations.operation: Create a server-side draft
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied recipient, subject and body
data_operations.data_scope: Recipient address, subject and plain-text body.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Microsoft Graph /me/messages for mailbox persistence; status, subject, recipient and shortened ID return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: draft with recipient and subject present. This path creates a draft rather than requesting delivery.

data_operations.operation: Request mail transmission
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied mail content or server-held messages/drafts
data_operations.data_scope: send submits recipient, subject and body; reply submits a target message and comment; forward submits a target message, recipient and optional comment; send-draft references an existing draft.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Microsoft Graph sendMail, reply, forward or send endpoints; intended recipients are TO for send/forward, draft recipients for send-draft, and service-resolved reply recipients for reply. Status or errors return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: The corresponding sending command, with required arguments and identifier resolution where applicable. Actual delivery and server-composed content are not verified by the source.

data_operations.operation: Change message state, categories and folder placement
data_operations.source: Caller-selected message IDs, flags, labels and folder names; existing target categories
data_operations.data_scope: Read status, flag status, category arrays and destination folder IDs. categorize fetches categories during its broad lookup and again for the target. Bulk paths repeat identifier lookup and mutation for each argument.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Microsoft Graph mailbox state; projected status returns to the caller. Bulk mutation response bodies are discarded locally.
data_operations.condition: mark-read, mark-unread, flag, unflag, categorize, uncategorize, move, archive, delete or bulk commands. delete and bulk-delete move messages to deleteditems; they do not request permanent erasure.

data_operations.operation: Read category/folder metadata and change folders
data_operations.source: Graph folder and master-category collections; caller-supplied folder names
data_operations.data_scope: Folder identifiers, names and counts; category names, colors and shortened IDs. Creation submits a display name and optional resolved parent. Deletion submits a resolved folder ID.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local lookup and caller output; Graph stores created folders and receives folder DELETE requests.
data_operations.condition: folders, categories, create-folder or delete-folder; folder lookups also support move. Server-side recovery and effects on folder contents are undocumented.

data_operations.operation: Use existing inferred message classifications
data_operations.source: Graph inferenceClassification filters
data_operations.data_scope: Focused/other membership and selected message identifiers, subjects, senders and dates. The script consumes the service classification rather than computing it.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authenticated Graph query; classified message results return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: focused or other command.

data_operations.operation: Infer a thread-search keyword
data_operations.source: Selected message subject
data_operations.data_scope: A subject with reply/forward prefixes removed; its longest word, or a fallback first word, becomes a search term. Up to 20 matching messages supply subjects, senders, dates and shortened IDs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Keyword sent to Graph search; keyword and result metadata returned to the caller.
data_operations.condition: thread after resolving the target. This is heuristic association, not a demonstrated conversation-membership query.

data_operations.operation: List calendar events and calendars
data_operations.source: Graph calendar event, calendarView and calendars endpoints
data_operations.data_scope: Event subjects, times, locations and IDs; events/week also request isAllDay but do not output it. Today/week send UTC date windows and request Europe/Madrid output. Calendar listing outputs name, color, editability and shortened ID from an unprojected response.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Graph receives date queries and timezone preference; local scripts return projected results to the caller.
data_operations.condition: events, today, week or calendars. events sorts descending by start and supplies no future-time filter. The fixed timezone is a configuration choice, not evidence of the user's location.

data_operations.operation: Read event details and derive a body excerpt
data_operations.source: Resolved Graph calendar event
data_operations.data_scope: Unprojected event response; output includes subject, times, location, attendee email addresses, online-meeting flag, join link and up to 500 locally processed body characters.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local curl/jq processing; projected details return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Calendar read after identifier resolution.

data_operations.operation: Persist, update or delete calendar events
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied subject, dates, location or update field; local clock for quick creation
data_operations.data_scope: Creation sends subject, start/end and optional location with Europe/Madrid timezone. quick derives a one-hour interval. Updates submit one supported field; deletion references the resolved event ID.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Microsoft Graph calendar storage and DELETE endpoint; projected status or errors return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: create, quick, update or delete with applicable arguments and successful lookup. A DELETE request does not establish permanent server-side erasure.

data_operations.operation: Infer availability from returned events
data_operations.source: Caller time range and Graph calendarView response
data_operations.data_scope: Requested interval plus event subjects, starts and ends. The script infers free when the returned value has zero elements; otherwise it reports busy and event subjects.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Graph receives the interval; the local process receives event details; availability and, when busy, subjects return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: free with both dates supplied. Complete availability cannot be established from this first-response length check alone.

potential_excess.data_scope: Event subjects and start/end properties fetched for an availability check; subjects are also returned when busy.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Graph calendarView response to the local script; event subjects additionally cross the stdout boundary to the caller.
potential_excess.condition: free, especially when matching events exist.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document requires checking availability, not revealing event titles.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Query the requested interval and determine availability. The query itself is necessary; its event detail scope may be excessive.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a supported minimal availability or event-existence response and return status plus the requested interval, omitting titles and unused time properties.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve correct interval coverage and handle paging, errors and availability semantics; API support for a narrower response is unresolved.

potential_excess.data_scope: Subjects, senders, dates and IDs of unrelated messages matching a word derived from the target subject.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Graph search results enter the local script and are returned to the caller as thread results.
potential_excess.condition: thread when other conversations contain the selected keyword.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The command describes listing the same conversation/thread; longest-word search is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve messages belonging to the selected conversation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use an exact conversation-membership query if supported, or validate membership before presenting results as a thread.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain genuine thread messages and suffix compatibility; the supplied source does not establish a supported exact-thread API.

potential_excess.data_scope: Potential message metadata outside the Inbox.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The /me/messages response enters the local script and its projected results reach the caller.
potential_excess.condition: inbox if the unrestricted messages endpoint includes messages from other folders.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry command and implementation comment promise an Inbox listing, but the request has no Inbox-folder restriction.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: List the requested number of latest Inbox messages.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Scope the messages request to the Inbox folder while retaining the existing field projection and count.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Confirm the folder-scoped endpoint's behavior; retain all-mail searches on commands whose purpose requires them.

potential_excess.data_scope: Past-event subjects, dates, locations and identifiers potentially included in an upcoming-events result.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Graph calendar/events response to the local script and projected caller output.
potential_excess.condition: events when the unfiltered response contains past events.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document and code comment specify upcoming events; the request has no future-time restriction.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: List the requested count of upcoming events.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Apply an appropriate future-time boundary and ordering before retrieving results.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Define treatment of ongoing and recurring events and preserve the requested count and timezone behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated collections of up to 100 message IDs, or repeated folder/attachment listings.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Repeated Graph-to-local-process response boundaries; failure paths then output available names.
potential_excess.condition: Multiple bulk targets with reusable lookup membership, or a failed folder/attachment name lookup while the collection remains unchanged.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Bulk mutation and helpful failure output are supported purposes. Re-fetching an unchanged collection is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve each target, perform each required mutation and preserve useful failure names.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse an in-memory identifier list within a stable batch and retain folder/attachment listings for failure output.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Refresh when concurrent changes or moves affect lookup membership or IDs. Keep per-target mutations and selected attachment-content retrieval.

potential_excess.data_scope: Category labels on up to 100 messages during target-ID resolution.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Graph response to the local categorize process; those labels are discarded by the ID-only jq projection.
potential_excess.condition: categorize requests id,categories, then separately retrieves the selected message's categories.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Adding a category requires the target's existing labels, not other messages' labels.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve the target ID and retrieve its existing categories before updating.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove categories from the initial collection projection and keep the target-only categories request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain existing target labels and suffix resolution. This narrows extra data in a necessary lookup rather than deleting the necessary target read.

potential_excess.data_scope: Attachment properties outside listing/lookup needs, potentially including non-target content if the service returns it by default.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Unprojected Graph attachment collections enter local curl/jq before name filtering or output projection.
potential_excess.condition: attachments or download, if collection responses include additional properties or content.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Listing needs metadata; downloading needs the selected attachment's content.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain listing metadata or resolve the requested attachment, then fetch and save its content.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Request only id,name,size,contentType for listing and id,name for download lookup where supported; retain the selected content request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Confirm collection projection behavior. The source does not establish that contentBytes is returned in a collection, so the selected-content GET is not unconditionally redundant.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unused isAllDay values and any default event, calendar, folder or mutation-response properties outside the fields actually used.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Graph responses enter local curl/jq; unused properties are discarded rather than necessarily reaching the caller.
potential_excess.condition: events/week request isAllDay without using it; unprojected reads or mutations return additional properties, if any.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These commands need their displayed fields, lookup fields or mutation status. Local projection does not narrow data received from Graph.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep required reads and mutations, displayed details and error handling.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove unused selected fields; apply endpoint-supported field projections or minimal mutation responses.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Verify endpoint support. Full body fields may remain necessary for the existing locally transformed excerpts unless an equivalent bounded server response exists.

potential_excess.data_scope: CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET and REFRESH_TOKEN loaded for get/test/help paths; the existing ACCESS_TOKEN loaded for refresh.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local token-manager process memory only; unnecessary remote disclosure is not established.
potential_excess.condition: Credential loading occurs before command dispatch.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: get/test need ACCESS_TOKEN; refresh uses client credentials and REFRESH_TOKEN; usage output needs neither.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Load each command's required credential types and preserve the documented token output.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Move credential reads into their applicable command branches.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep refresh persistence, authentication checks and intended get output.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Azure application permission registration, not a demonstrated profile-data transfer.
potential_excess.condition: Automated permission addition succeeds, or the manual configuration is followed.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: User.Read is explicitly documented, but packaged mail/calendar operations contain no profile endpoint call and authorization scope strings omit it.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Authorize supported mail/calendar actions and continued access.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit User.Read registration unless a separately required profile feature depends on it.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Confirm no external deployment dependency requires profile access; do not infer an existing User.Read grant or profile read from registration alone.

unknowns: Blocking confirmation of conditional response excess: supplied source does not define Graph default response fields, attachment collection content, nested-property scope, or endpoint support for narrower/minimal responses. Unselected properties and attachment bytes must not be assumed.

Blocking confirmation of exact message/calendar coverage: external endpoint semantics, actual mailbox contents, paging and concurrent changes are unavailable. Source shows bounded ID scans, an unrestricted inbox messages query, an unfiltered upcoming-events query and a first-response availability check.

Blocking confirmation of delivery, persistence and deletion effects: Microsoft-side retention, logs, sent copies, reply/forward composition, notifications, folder-content consequences and recovery or permanent-erasure behavior are undocumented.
Azure CLI internals, authentication caches, telemetry and the external effects of credential reset/logout are not supplied. Only the invoked operations and locally captured outputs can be attributed.
Browser, terminal, shell-history and downstream caller retention are unspecified. Stdout results may remain with their caller; no additional recipient or onward transmission is established.
All packaged source files were reviewed. Runtime grants, response contents, operation success and deployment-specific dependencies remain unresolved; no execution or external retrieval was performed.
